summary: Backend-only regression + new-feature testing for the v7 pre-cut vegetable catalog (62 Freshncut SKUs added with sku + local_name fields, regex-based case-insensitive cut_type filter, and expanded /products search over name/local_name/sku). Added a new focused test module test_cutveg_catalog.py (15 tests, all pass). Refreshed 4 stale v3-era regression tests in test_freshcuts_api.py to align with the v7 seed (~90 products, 65 cut-veg, product named 'Onion' not 'Onions', variant cuts like 'sliced-full' now match 'sliced' filter). Full suite: 65/65 tests pass in ~5s. Every review-request checklist item is verified end-to-end against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 840 lines (was 695) — well beyond the 700-line guideline. Strongly recommend extracting CUTVEG_CATALOG (~65 lines), _CUTVEG_IMAGE_BY_NAME (~65 lines) and _build_cutveg_products() into a separate module e.g. backend/seed_cutveg.py. Non-blocking, style/maintainability only.

The /api/products endpoint applies the cut_type regex directly on the raw user string ({"$regex": cut_type, "$options": "i"}). Untrusted regex characters (e.g. q='(((') will hit MongoDB as-is and either error out or produce broad matches. Suggest re.escape() before passing to $regex, or Pydantic-validate cut_type against a known set. Same applies to the q parameter in the $or search.

Product model has sku: Optional[str] = None but there is no uniqueness constraint or index on sku. Two seeds with the same SKU would silently coexist. Consider adding a unique index (or an application-level guard in the seeder) so admins uploading CSVs cannot introduce duplicate SKUs.

SEED_PRODUCTS has grown to ~90 entries embedded as Python literals. If the source of truth is the Excel file the user provided, consider persisting it as a JSON/CSV asset under backend/seed_data/ and loading at startup; makes future updates diffable.

New tests to reuse for future catalog changes live in /app/backend/tests/test_cutveg_catalog.py.
